calls.content:
DECISION

**(1) Relisting the dog-groomer sheet at £12 for another 21 days with nothing changed: NO.**

*Why not:*
- **Recorded result:** it was listed at £12 from 1 to 21 Oct 2026, with no ads. It got 212 views, 3 favourites and 0 sales, and cost £0.20. This was a simulated result from the test environment, not a real market result, and no revenue came from it.
- **Views were fine, the offer wasn't.** If 1.5% of viewers were buying, 0 sales from 212 views would happen only about 4% of the time. At 1% it would happen about 12% of the time. So the real rate is probably below 1%. Another 21 days at similar traffic would likely bring about 0 to 2 sales, still short of the goal of 5 or more.
- **Buyers raised two objections that a relist can't fix:**
  - They asked whether it files to HMRC under Making Tax Digital (MTD). A spreadsheet can't.
  - Their accountant gives them a free sheet. My competitor check (attempt 8db0ca8f-0000-4000-8000-000000000003) only looked at paid listings, so it missed this.
- **The early research doesn't support demand either.** The forum pain was real (8db0ca8f-0000-4000-8000-000000000002, 41 replies), but nobody said they had bought anything. The two competitors' low sales (14 and 6, from attempt …0003) look like a sign of weak demand, not an opening.
- **Stopping early was already decided.** Goal g1 was closed as not validated: the listing ran 21 of the planned 45 days and I stopped because of the two objections. A second 21 days would make 42 days, still not the full 45. More importantly, it would test the same thing again with no new question.

*Terms:*
- **Cost ceiling:** £0.
- **Time limit:** not applicable.
- **Kill criteria:** already met; the idea is closed as specified.
- **What would reopen it:** a changed offer based on new evidence. For example, if official gov.uk figures show many groomers are below the MTD income threshold, I could aim at that group, and that would be a different test. Separately, I don't know whether the original listing is still live under its 4-month listing fee.

**(2) Mobile-hairdresser lead: do the three free checks first. Don't list anything yet and don't request any spending.**

*Evidence so far:*
- **Forum** (b2c03233-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, https://forum.hairpros.example/t/mobile-hair-accounts): 33 replies about mileage and product costs. People use notebooks or banking apps. One will switch to MTD software, one has a free template from their accountant, and one would try "something simple if it was cheap". Nobody mentions paying.
- **Stallhub search** (b2c03233-0000-4000-8000-000000000002): 5 listings at £4–15. The best seller is £7 with 31 sales and 9 reviews; the £15 listing has 2 sales.
- **Search volume** (b2c03233-0000-4000-8000-000000000003): about 430 UK searches a month, give or take 40%.
- **What I expect to earn per sale:** from the fee schedule in force since 1 Oct 2026 (4b75d0ab-0000-4000-8000-000000000001), a £6 sale nets about £5.02. A £7 sale nets about £5.89. The £0.20 listing fee comes on top.
- **Warning from the dog-groomer test:** the same two objections showed up in this forum thread too.

*Next step: three free checks, stopping at the first one that fails:*
1. **Read the £7 best seller's 9 reviews.** If they show no gap that mobile-specific features (mileage between clients, product costs) would fill, stop.
2. **Check the MTD income thresholds on an official source.** If most mobile hairdressers must use MTD software by April 2027, drop the idea.
3. **Re-fetch Stallhub's fee page.** If a £6 sale would net less than about £4.50, reconsider.

*Cost ceilings:*
- **The checks:** £0 cash, and at most about £0.50 of AI and research usage.
- **Test, if all three checks pass:**
  - **Cost:** at most £1 cash for listing fees (no ads) plus about £3 of AI usage.
  - **Time limit:** 30 days.
  - **Approval:** I would first ask the owner for approval through request_spend.
  - **Success:** at least 3 sales at £6 or more, at least 1% of viewers buying, and at least one buyer saying the mobile features mattered.
  - **Kill criteria:** 150 or more views with 0 sales (early stop allowed); 0 sales by day 30; or 2 or more buyers raising the MTD or free-template objections.

*What's missing:*
- The link to the best seller's listing and its reviews. The search page may have it, but it isn't recorded.
- The official MTD thresholds: my last gov.uk fetch returned a 404 error.
- How long the best seller took to reach its 31 sales.
- Stallhub's identity checks for sellers.
- Whether the owner has a real Stallhub seller account. The dog-groomer test was simulated, so this is unconfirmed.
- An approved payment destination ID from the owner, needed before any listing-fee request.

Nothing was spent. The ledger still shows £99.50 cash and £0 revenue.

knowledge.value:
I will not spend anything until new evidence supports a direction. Options to research cheaply:
(a) MTD angle: buyers ask about MTD. Filing software itself needs HMRC recognition and is a high barrier (probably unsuitable). A lower-capital idea: a guide or setup service on which recognised MTD software or bridging tool suits small groomers. I would need proof people will pay, not just that they ask questions.
(b) Sell through accountants rather than against them: they are the channel that already hands out sheets. Unvalidated.
(c) Go back to opportunity discovery.
TEST DESIGN LESSONS for any next test:
- Check free substitutes (accountants, gov.uk, free tools), not only paid listings.
- Treat a small, low-selling competitor as a demand warning, not an opening.
- Before building, check which features are required to buy (e.g. compliance).
- Run the full planned window, or state in advance when stopping early is allowed.

STATUS at 2026-09-29: research is done. O2 chosen (goal g1 open). Nothing built, no spend requested, no revenue.
UNCERTAINTIES:
- Small market: the best existing listing has only 14 sales.
- Stated vs real demand: forum posters are self-selected; one said they would pay £10–15, but none mentioned actually buying.
- Retention: one poster gave up on a template after a week.
- MTD scope: don't overclaim.
- Search volume is a modelled estimate (±40%).
- Stallhub seller KYC rules are unchecked.
NEXT STEPS: (1) Check Stallhub seller/identity requirements. (2) Ask the owner for the account and listing-fee approval. (3) Build the sheet in the workspace. (4) Track sales from launch.
